Who sets and who collects the tax

Two offices split the work. The State Department of Assessments and Taxation (SDAT) decides what the property is worth. The county's Department of Finance sends the bill and takes the payment. Each level of government sets its own rate, so one bill can carry county, state and other charges.

OfficeRoleContact
SDAT Montgomery County Assessment OfficeValues, notices, appeals30 W. Gude Drive, Suite 400, Rockville; (240) 314-4510
County Department of FinanceBilling and collection, tax lien sale101 Monroe Street, 15th Floor, Rockville; 240-777-8860
MC311Tax questions(240) 777-0311

Expect the bill in July or August, covering the fiscal year that begins July 1. Finance also offers a tax credit for residents 65 and older and for retired military service members, plus an online portal to view or pay real property bills.

The county rate

The county's general property tax rate was 1.0392 in both FY 2025 and FY 2026. It was 0.9905 in FY 2022, 0.9915 in FY 2023 and 1.0402 in FY 2024. These rates apply to assessed value, and the full bill also carries state and other charges. Special rates cover services the general rate does not fund, so a given street can pay more or less than the headline number.

The rate held flat for the year starting July 1, 2026, and yet plenty of homeowners saw a bigger bill. The next section explains why.

Why a bill can rise when the rate does not

Two changes pushed bills up in 2026: rising assessments and the end of a county credit. The Income Tax Offset Credit, shown on bills as the County Property Tax Credit, was $692 in levy year 2025. The County Council set it to $0 for 2026. It was not permanently repealed, and it only ever applied to owner-occupied principal residences.

Average homeowners faced about $23 more per month from higher assessments. If the council sets the credit above zero again, a homeowner needs a homestead application on file with SDAT by May 1, 2027 for it to appear on July 1, 2027 bills.

Because the council sets the credit anew each year, last year's bill says little about what a buyer will owe. Hand over the current bill instead.

The assessment cycle and the homestead cap

SDAT reappraises every property once every three years, so about one-third of Montgomery County homes get a new value each year. If the market value on the notice looks wrong to you, appeal it. Filing with SDAT is always free.

On a principal residence, the taxable assessment can climb at most 10% a year, or 5% in the Town of Kensington. Only owner-occupied principal residences get the homestead credit, and each county or town picks its own percentage from 0% to 10%. The 10% cap costs the county an estimated 0.4% of its assessable base in the fiscal 2026 table.

A purchase resets things: the cap is not applied in the first year, so an owner of many years and a new neighbor can be taxed on different figures. Your buyer's first bill may therefore look different from yours.

How to appeal your assessment

An appeal of a reassessment must be filed within 45 days of the date on the SDAT notice. The process has three levels, and the Appeals Board charges nothing.

  1. The Supervisor's level, an informal hearing with an assessor that usually lasts about 15 minutes. SDAT supplies a property worksheet and area sales listing beforehand.
  2. The Property Tax Assessment Appeals Board, with one board in each of the 24 jurisdictions, appointed by the Governor and independent of SDAT. Your request is due 30 days after the Supervisor's final notice.
  3. The Maryland Tax Court, which hears the case fresh and requires an in-person appearance. You have 30 days after the Board's order.

Buyers get a separate 60 day appeal window from the transfer date, though only when the sale falls after January 1 and before July 1 and the deed is already in the land records. If you close in that stretch, mention the option to your buyer.

Due dates and relief programs

A principal residence can be paid in two installments, September 30 and December 31. Anyone else follows the annual schedule: due July 1 without interest, overdue after October 1.

Splitting the payment can cost extra, since a local government may add up to 1.65% of the second installment as a service charge. Fees on the same bill, such as water and sewer, may be due with the first installment.

Ask about two relief programs. The state's Homeowners' Property Tax Credit depends on income and requires a fresh application each year; SDAT can give you the current deadline. The county senior credit equals 50% of the combined state credit and county supplement for residents 65 and older, and it also requires the state application.

Sell as-isNo repairs, no cleaning and no showings. We buy Montgomery County houses in any condition.See My Cash Offer →

If taxes go unpaid

The county turns unpaid taxes into a lien and sells it at an annual sealed-bid sale in June. To keep a property out of the sale, pay everything owed, with interest and penalties, no later than the last business day before it.

You still own the house after the sale, and you may redeem the lien until a Circuit Court order ends that right. Redemption interest on the certificate is 6% a year for owner-occupied properties and 20% a year for non-owner-occupied ones. A purchaser can seek foreclosure after 6 months, or 9 months for owner-occupied homes.

For scale, in the 2024 sales the county advertised 2,092 properties in the first notice, offered 1,327 for sale and sold 1,029 liens, and 1,184 were redeemed before foreclosure in FY 2024. The state also runs a Homeowner Protection Program and a Tax Sale Ombudsman, reachable at (410) 767-4994, for limited-income, elderly and disabled homeowners.

Taxes at closing

Back taxes are a lien, and the lien must be cleared for the title to pass cleanly. Ask the Department of Finance for a payoff, since penalties and interest continue until the balance is paid.

Closing also brings recordation and transfer tax, which the county reshaped in 2023. The guide to Montgomery County land records covers those charges. Deferred taxes under the optional program for owners 65 and older become a lien and are repaid when the property is transferred.

With a cash buyer, no lender is waiting in the background, and the payoff is taken out of the price at closing. Bring the current bill and your payoff letter to the title company so nothing is missed.

Frequently asked questions

Who do I call about a Montgomery County property tax bill?

Start with MC311 at (240) 777-0311 or the Department of Finance at 240-777-8860. Questions about a value or appeal go to the SDAT Montgomery County assessment office at (240) 314-4510.

How long do I have to appeal a Montgomery County assessment?

Forty-five days from the SDAT notice date. Someone who bought from January 1 up to July 1 gets 60 days from the transfer, as soon as the deed is recorded.

When are Montgomery County property taxes due?

A principal residence can split the bill into September 30 and December 31 payments, and the second can include a service charge of up to 1.65%.

Is there a cap on how fast my Montgomery County assessment can rise?

Yes, for a principal residence: 10% a year, or 5% in the Town of Kensington. A purchase resets it, so the first year after a sale is not capped.

What is the redemption interest after a Montgomery County tax lien sale?

It is 6% a year for owner-occupied properties and 20% a year for non-owner-occupied properties. Redemption stays possible until a court order forecloses it.

Baltimore County versus Baltimore City

Baltimore County wraps around the independent city of Baltimore without including it. Towson is the county seat, and the 2020 census counted 854,535 residents across 682 square miles. The city left the county in 1851, so the offices described here serve only properties on the county side of the line. Baltimore City runs its own tax and land records offices. Communities range from dense Dundalk, Catonsville and Essex to a rural north, so lot size and property type vary widely.

2026 reassessment

SDAT revalued the county for January 1, 2026, and full cash value rose 12.1 percent over the three years from January 1, 2023.

MeasureJan. 1, 2023 valueJan. 1, 2026 valueChange
Combined value$47.17 billion$52.88 billionUp 12.1%
Residential$34.02 billion$38.22 billionUp 12.4%
Commercial$13.16 billion$14.65 billionUp 11.3%

About 85.93 percent of residential properties went up. An increase phases in evenly over three years, and a decrease applies fully in the 2026 tax year. The window to appeal is 45 days from the Notice of Assessment. SDAT hears it first, and further appeals go to the county board and then the Maryland Tax Court. SDAT keeps an office at 300 East Joppa Road, Room 602, in Towson.

How and when to pay

Real property tax bills are issued July 1. Owner-occupied homes can pay in two installments, the first through September 30 and the second through December 31. The county's schedule shows July 1 and December 1 as installment dates, with September 30 and December 31 as the last days to pay with no penalty or interest.

Owner-occupied homes and small businesses can use two-payment billing, provided the owner lives in the house for over six months out of twelve. Each installment covers half of the state and county tax, half of the homestead and homeowners' credits, and half of any metropolitan charges. If a mortgage escrow pays the first installment, no December bill is issued, but you still need to make sure the second payment goes out on time. To remain an annual payer, tell the mortgage company 60 days before the tax year.

The Office of Budget and Finance is at 400 Washington Avenue, Room 150, Towson, open Monday through Friday, 8 a.m. to 4:30 p.m. Call 410-887-2404 or email financeinfo@baltimorecountymd.gov.

The tax sale calendar

An unpaid bill can end with the property sold at the annual June tax sale. A missed first installment makes the account delinquent, and so does any balance left after December 31.

  • February: delinquent notices go out, and partial payments are taken until month end.
  • End of February: last day to apply for the Hardship Installment Payment Program and avoid a sale.
  • March 1: a Final Tax Sale notice gives 30 days to pay.
  • Around May 1: properties scheduled for sale are posted on the county website.
  • June: the annual tax sale.

The county gives an owner six months from the sale date to redeem. Ask the county and a lawyer how redemption and interest apply to your account. Partial payments do not stop interest, though they usually reduce what builds up.

Lien certificates

A lien certificate shows the status of unpaid taxes or charges on a property account, and the county requires one before any real property transfer. The fee is $55, payable to Baltimore County, Maryland, with a completed application. In most cases every unpaid tax and charge must be paid before the transfer goes through.

Order it early. The Transfer Tax Section at 410-887-2416 answers account questions, and the Liens Section of the Clerk of the Court at 410-887-2622 handles legal liens that show up on credit reports. Our Baltimore County land records guide covers the recording side of the same sale.

Selling a rental property

Every rental in the county needs a rental license or an exemption license under County Code Section 35-5-201, and the owner needs the license in hand before a tenant moves in. The rule covers dwellings of six or fewer units, short-term rentals included, and buildings with seven or more units.

  • Licenses last three years and can be renewed for further three-year terms.
  • Short-term rental licenses cost $300 per unit.
  • For seven or more units, an owner with fewer than three code violations in three years may file a self-certification affidavit. Otherwise 10 percent of units are inspected.
  • Within one mile of the main Towson University campus, licenses may be restricted where the rental rate is 30 percent or more.

Rental Housing Registration is at 111 West Chesapeake Avenue, Room 216, Towson, 410-887-6060. If you are selling a house with tenants, check that the license is current first.

Delinquent accounts and what to do first

If your account has gone delinquent, timing matters more than anything else. Partial payments are accepted through the end of February, and the Hardship Installment Payment Program application closes at the end of that month. After March 1 the clock is the 30 days on the Final Tax Sale notice, and by about May 1 the county posts the properties scheduled for the June sale.

Gather your bills, any notices you received and your mortgage statement before you call 410-887-2404. Tell the office whether the home is owner-occupied, since that decides whether the two-installment schedule applied to you. If a mortgage escrow was supposed to cover the first installment, ask the lender to confirm it was paid, because no December bill is issued in that case.

Selling with taxes owed

Because the county wants a lien certificate before transfer, plan to learn your balance early. The title company pays what is owed from the sale proceeds. If you have already received a Final Tax Sale notice, you have 30 days to pay from the March 1 mailing, so contact the Office of Budget and Finance right away.

  1. Order the lien certificate and check the amount.
  2. Ask the Transfer Tax Section whether any legal lien is attached.
  3. If you rent the house, confirm the license is current.
  4. Give the certificate to the title company so it can plan the payoff.

Keep every receipt and confirmation from the county, since the title company may ask for proof of what you have already paid, and note that a legal lien showing on a credit report is handled by the Clerk of the Court rather than the tax office. Clearing both before closing avoids surprises at the table.

A cash sale as is can move quickly. Send us the address and your balance, and we will tell you what we can offer.

Frequently asked questions

When are Baltimore County property taxes due?

Bills are issued July 1, and the first installment of a semiannual bill is payable through September 30. The second is payable through December 31 without penalty or interest.

Who can pay Baltimore County property tax in two installments?

Owner-occupied residential property and small businesses qualify. The owner must live in the home more than six months of a 12-month period.

How much is a Baltimore County lien certificate?

The fee is $55, payable to Baltimore County, Maryland, with a completed application. One is required before any real property transfer.

When is the Baltimore County tax sale?

The annual sale is in June. The county mails a Final Tax Sale notice on March 1 and posts properties on its website around May 1.

How long do I have to appeal a Baltimore County assessment?

You have 45 days from the Notice of Assessment to appeal to SDAT. The appeal then continues to the county appeals board and the Maryland Tax Court.

Anne Arundel County at a glance

Just south of Baltimore, Anne Arundel County fronts the Chesapeake Bay, and its seat Annapolis doubles as Maryland's capital. About 588,261 people lived here in 2020. Water covers 173 of the county's 588 square miles (29 percent), which is why creeks, rivers and shoreline lots define so much of the housing. Fort Meade, BWI airport and state government keep buyers coming, and commuters reach Baltimore and Washington by road, light rail or MARC.

The latest reassessment

The state assessments office, SDAT, revalued the county as of January 1, 2026. Here is how much value moved over the three years.

Measure (Jan. 1, 2023 to Jan. 1, 2026)Anne Arundel County
Combined full cash value$46.52 billion to $53.53 billion (up 15.1%)
Residential value$31.23 billion to $36.24 billion (up 16.0%)
Commercial value$15.28 billion to $17.29 billion (up 13.1%)
Residential properties that rose in value98.98%

Higher values are spread in equal steps over three years, while a drop applies in full for the 2026 tax year. To contest a value, you have 45 days from the date on the Notice of Assessment. Start with SDAT, then go to the county's Property Tax Assessment Appeals Board, and last to the Maryland Tax Court. On a principal residence, the homestead credit holds down how fast taxable assessment can grow: 10 percent is the state ceiling, and some local governments set it lower.

Due dates and payment options

The annual bill goes out in July to the mailing address SDAT has on file. It is payable without interest starting July 1 and must be settled by September 30. If you live in the house as your principal residence, you may pay in two halves, the first by September 30 and the second by December 31.

The fiscal year 2027 bill, covering July 1, 2026 to June 30, 2027, carries a 0.87 percent service charge on whatever is left for the second installment. Maryland lets local governments charge up to 1.65 percent, so this county stays under the limit. A single payment by September 30 avoids the charge altogether.

  • The state portion is $0.112 per $100 of taxable assessment.
  • Addresses inside the City of Annapolis add $0.738 per $100.
  • If a lender escrows your taxes and you prefer a single annual payment, notify the lender by May 1.
  • A homestead credit application filed by December 31 starts working July 1 of the next year.

Before you estimate what you owe, ask the Real Property Tax Division which county rate applies to your address.

Who to contact

The Real Property Tax Division, 44 Calvert Street, Room 110, Annapolis, answers billing questions. Reach it Monday through Friday, 8:00 a.m. to 4:30 p.m., at (410) 222-1736 or realproperty@aacounty.org. Values and ownership records sit with SDAT.

  • Finance Department customer service: (410) 222-1144.
  • Land Records, for deeds and liens: (410) 222-1425.
  • SDAT, to change ownership or a mailing address: (410) 974-5709.
  • Cashier's offices, including the one in Glen Burnie, are open Monday through Friday, 8:00 a.m. to 4:00 p.m. Outside those hours, drop a sealed check in the yellow box and it is handled the next business day.

Did you pay a bill on a house you have already sold? Ask the office about a refund. Credits left after a bill is adjusted are returned as quickly as possible.

Transfer and recordation taxes

Recording a deed here costs a county recordation tax of $7.00 per thousand of value, with the base rounded up to the next $500. The county transfer tax is 1.0 percent for prices through $999,999.99 and 1.5 percent from $1 million up. The Recordation and Transfer Tax Division collects both and must endorse any instrument that could be taxed before it goes on record.

Make checks payable to Anne Arundel County. The state's transfer tax and recording fees run through the Land Records Office at (410) 222-1425, which also accepts e-recording. Refund claim forms for both taxes and an affidavit for certain transactions are posted by the county. The sales contract decides who pays which tax, so have your title company list each charge before you accept an offer.

Waterfront sellers and the Critical Area

Land and water within 1,000 feet of tidal waters make up the Critical Area, and the rules can limit what a buyer is allowed to do with a lot.

  • The Buffer extends 100 feet landward from tidal waters, tributary stream banks and tidal wetland boundaries. Disturbing it generally takes an approved variance.
  • Removing any tree or vegetation, even a dead tree, requires an approved Vegetation Management Plan.
  • Grading disturbances over 5,000 square feet need a grading permit.
  • In limited development and resource conservation areas, impervious surface is capped at 15 to 31 percent of the site.

The county's Critical Area Planner of the Day is at the Heritage Complex, 2664 Riva Road, Annapolis, (410) 222-7960. Own a pier, deck or bulkhead near the water? Gather its permits before you list, and ask the title company whether any disclosure applies.

Sell as-isNo repairs, no cleaning and no showings. We buy Anne Arundel County houses in any condition.See My Cash Offer →

If taxes go unpaid

Tax left unpaid turns into a lien, and the county can auction that lien at its June tax sale on a date the Controller picks. You still own the house afterward. The winning bidder gets a tax lien certificate and may foreclose if the debt is never cleared.

Ahead of the sale the collector has to mail you a notice at least 30 days before the first advertisement, which then runs weekly for four weeks. The buyer can start foreclosure six months after the sale, or nine for an owner-occupied home, and the certificate dies if nothing is filed within two years. To redeem, you pay interest of 1.5 percent per month, so every month of delay adds to the payoff.

Homeowners with limited income, or who are elderly or disabled, may be eligible for the state's Homeowner Protection Program. The State Tax Sale Ombudsman sees people by appointment at 123 Market Place, Baltimore.

Selling with taxes owed

Owing money to the county does not block a sale, as long as the balance is cleared by closing. Get the amount from the Real Property Tax Division, and move before the June tax sale if you are behind. The title company can wire the county out of your proceeds.

  1. Request a payoff figure for each open bill.
  2. Collect permits for any waterfront structures and any Critical Area approvals.
  3. Have the title company spell out the recordation and transfer taxes.
  4. Close, and the title company pays the county from the proceeds.

Our offers are for the house as it stands, so a worn bulkhead or an old deck is not something you have to fix first. Send the address by call or text and we will say what we can pay.

Frequently asked questions

When are Anne Arundel County property taxes due?

Payment without interest opens July 1 and closes September 30. A principal residence may be paid half by September 30 and half by December 31.

What is the semiannual service charge in Anne Arundel County?

It is 0.87 percent of the second installment balance for fiscal year 2027. One full payment by September 30 avoids it.

How do I appeal an Anne Arundel County assessment?

Send it to SDAT within 45 days of the Notice of Assessment. Still unhappy? Take it to the county appeals board, then the Maryland Tax Court.

What are the transfer tax rates in Anne Arundel County?

Transfer tax is 1.0 percent through $999,999.99 and 1.5 percent at $1 million or more. Recordation tax is $7.00 per thousand, rounded up to the next $500.

Does the Critical Area affect selling a house near the water?

It can. A lot within 1,000 feet of tidal water is in the Critical Area, with a 100 foot buffer plus vegetation and grading rules that a buyer needs to know about.

Frederick County market context

North-central Maryland holds Frederick County, part of the Washington metro region, and the city of Frederick is where its government sits. The 2020 census counted 271,717 people and the 2025 estimate is 302,883, growth driven by households moving out from the Washington area. Fort Detrick employs 10,827 people, and with the school system, hospital and research labs nearby, housing demand follows federal and research hiring.

The properties on the market range widely: city and suburban lots in and around Frederick, valley farms in the Middletown Valley, and mountain parcels near Catoctin Mountain Park and South Mountain. Town rules differ, so find out whether your address falls inside a municipality before you read a bill.

Due dates and discounts

Mailing happens in July, and bills are online by July 1. This is how annual and semiannual bills work.

Payment optionDue dateDiscount or penalty
Annual or first semiannual bill paid in JulySeptember 301 percent discount
Annual or first semiannual bill paid in AugustSeptember 30One-half percent discount
Second semiannual installmentDecember 31None listed
Unpaid accountFrom October 1Interest of 1 percent per month
  • Supplemental bills: mailed in August for June transfers and for state credits issued after the July billing. Supplemental and revised bills are due 30 days from issue.
  • Postmark rule: A mailed payment counts as of its USPS postmark if the postmark is on or before the last day of the month, and an online payment has to be submitted before midnight that day.

Skipping payment because no bill arrived is not an accepted excuse. Lenders receive an electronic file instead of paper, so if you escrow, pass any new construction bill to your lender yourself, since that bill is mailed only to the owner.

Where to pay and who to call

Treasury sits at 30 North Market Street in Frederick and is open weekdays, 8 a.m. until 4 p.m. The phone is 301-600-1111, and mail goes to 30 N. Market St., Frederick, MD 21701. At the counter you can hand over cash, a check, a money order or a card.

A vendor handles cards and charges 2.5 percent, none of which goes to the county. Lenders can use a mass payment option through the billing office.

Treasury also issues a Lien Certificate and a Tax Status Report on request. Ordering one before closing shows exactly what tax, if any, is still open.

Rates and local taxes

Outside any town, the county rate on real property was 1.1100 for each $100 of assessed value in fiscal 2025 and stays there in fiscal 2026. From fiscal 2022 through 2024 it was 1.0600. For both of the newer years the state's tables show no county transfer tax (0.0 percent) and a recordation figure of $7.00.

Towns levy a separate district tax that pays for streets, trash removal and police, and homestead caps vary from 0 percent to 10 percent by town. So a house inside a town costs more to carry than one outside.

Credits and deferrals

  • Senior Tax Credit: for older owners (65 and up) under the income limits, worth 20 percent of net county real property taxes.
  • Deferral program: for owners of at least five years who are 65 or older or totally disabled and meet income limits. Deferred amounts become a lien at 3 percent annual interest, which the title company pays off at closing.
  • Homestead Tax Credit: caps the yearly rise in taxable assessment on a principal residence and kicks in automatically after 12 months of living there. Call SDAT at 301-815-5350.
  • Homeowner's Property Tax Credit: income based for all ages, with applications due by September of the tax year.

If you use a deferral, ask Treasury for the balance with interest before you set a price, because it is deducted from what you walk away with.

How to appeal your assessment

Notices arrive about every three years, and in the two years between, a petition for review must be in by the first working day after January 1. The first-level hearing can be handled in writing, by phone, by video or in person. If the house changed hands between January 1 and June 30, the new owner has 60 days from the transfer, after the deed is recorded.

If you fall behind

Tax liens are sold online each spring. You keep possession while redeeming, and the right to redeem lasts until the Circuit Court forecloses it. Redemption costs no extra expenses like legal fees during the first four months on a non-owner-occupied property and the first seven months on an owner-occupied one. The certificate interest rate is 8 percent a year. Call 301-600-1111 for the redemption amount.

Rental condition falls under the 2024 International Property Maintenance Code, which the county's Division of Housing, 401 Sagner Avenue, enforces when someone complains. Complaints about properties inside the city of Frederick go to city inspectors at 301-600-3825.

Selling with taxes owed

A balance on the tax account is a title issue, not a deal breaker. The steps are short.

  1. Ask Treasury for a Lien Certificate or Tax Status Report, which shows what remains open on the account.
  2. Ask whether a municipal district tax or a supplemental bill is also outstanding, because those come on separate notices apart from the county's yearly bill.
  3. Give the certificate to your title company, which will pay Treasury from your proceeds on the closing date.
  4. If a deferral lien exists, add its balance and 3 percent interest to the payoff.

Timing matters as well. Interest of 1 percent a month keeps building from October 1, and lien sales come in the spring, so a fall closing is cheaper than one that drifts beyond the deadline, and a spring lien sale makes late delay costlier still. A house that needs repairs can be sold for cash as-is, and the tax payoff simply appears on the settlement statement with no repair negotiation beforehand. Bring the latest bill, any escrow statement and your deferral paperwork to the first call with the title company. If the property is inside a town, also ask Treasury whether the district tax is collected by the county or the town, so you pay the right office and get a receipt from each. Keep every receipt until the deed is recorded, because a buyer's attorney may ask to see proof that the account was current on the day of settlement.

When is Frederick County property tax due?

Annual bills and first installments are due September 30, second installments December 31. Unpaid accounts begin gaining 1 percent a month on October 1. Pay in July for a 1 percent discount, or in August for one-half percent.

How do I reach the Frederick County Treasury?

Phone 301-600-1111 or go to 30 North Market Street in Frederick on a weekday. Cash, checks, money orders and cards are all accepted.

What is the Frederick County property tax rate?

For the unincorporated county it is 1.1100 per $100 in fiscal 2025 and 2026. Municipalities add their own rates, so a house inside a town pays more.

Can I sell with unpaid property tax in Frederick County?

Yes. The title company settles the balance from your proceeds on closing day. Request a lien certificate or tax status report beforehand to pin the amount down.

Does Frederick County charge a transfer tax?

The state's local tax table shows a 0.0 percent county transfer tax and a $7.00 recordation figure for fiscal 2025 and 2026. State-level charges can still apply, so check the closing statement with the title company.

Howard County in brief

Central Maryland, between Baltimore and Washington, D.C., is where Howard County sits. Not one incorporated town exists inside it, so the county handles what a city would elsewhere. Columbia, a planned community founded in 1967 with roughly 100,000 residents, and Ellicott City, the county seat with 75,947 residents in 2020, are the names most sellers know.

Median household income was estimated at $124,042 in 2020, and the county school system runs 71 schools for about 49,000 students. With no town layer, a Howard deed goes through one county finance office rather than a town clerk first, which simplifies closing.

Ellicott City flood history

Several stream valleys converge on Ellicott City's historic core, which has flooded badly twice. On July 30, 2016 about 6 inches of rain fell in two hours and two people died. On May 27, 2018 more than 8 inches fell in two hours and one person died.

The county's answer was a plan costing roughly $140 million over five years, including a 15-foot-diameter tunnel through about 1,600 feet of hillside. It aimed to bring street flooding down from more than four feet to under one, not to stop flooding altogether. Building removals and construction ran from January 2024 into summer 2024, and renovation of six remaining buildings was still underway in February 2025.

If your house is in or near the historic district, buyers and lenders will ask about flood history and insurance. The same question comes up for homes beside streams elsewhere in the county, so assemble your insurance declarations and any claim records before you list.

Who bills the tax and the rate

Bills come from the county Department of Finance each July 1, while SDAT sets the assessed value. Finance answers at 410-313-2062.

SDAT's 2026 to 2027 table lists a county real property rate of $1.0440 per $100 and a State rate of $0.1120, with a 5% homestead credit cap and no municipal rate. A special rate for services the general rate does not fund can add to the total, so read your own tax account for the full bill.

  • Payment portal: MuniciPay for the current bill.
  • Prior-year bills and history: the county's self-service site.
  • E-check fee: $1.00. Card fee: 2.35%, with a $2.00 minimum.
  • Allow three to five business days for processing.

Many taxpayers can choose semiannual payments. Call Finance to ask which credits you qualify for, and whether any credit on your account ends when you sell. If you are mid-year when the sale closes, the title company usually adjusts the bill between you and the buyer, so having the current amount and payment status in front of you keeps that adjustment accurate. Pay any open balance before listing if you can, since a clean account makes the title search quicker.

How to appeal your assessment

To contest a reassessment you must file within 45 days of the notice date. SDAT mails notices on a three-year cycle, which means one arrives every third year and none in between.

Step one is an informal Supervisor's hearing of about 15 minutes. Still unhappy? The local Property Tax Assessment Appeals Board takes appeals filed within 30 days, and the Maryland Tax Court takes them 30 days after the board's order. Neither one costs anything to file.

Between notices, a petition for review can be filed up to the first working day after January 1. A house that transfers after January 1 and before July 1 gives its new owner 60 days from the transfer to appeal.

Transfer and recordation costs

The Clerk of the Circuit Court's Land Records page lists a State transfer tax of 0.5%, a county transfer tax of 1.25% and a recordation tax of $2.50 per $500 of consideration.

Consideration is not limited to cash and can include debt a buyer assumes. Misstating it on a deed is a crime under the Tax-Property Article.

Overdue tax and the tax sale

One tax sale happens each year, in June, and the Howard County Times carries the list of delinquent properties for at least four weeks first.

Howard has the shortest wait of any county in the state's tax sale report: a property can be offered when it is 30 days overdue. In 2024 the county advertised 1,103 parcels, offered 349 and sold 308, with 173 of those owner-occupied. Interest runs 1.5% a month on the county share and 1% on the State share, and redemption interest is 18% a year.

What bidders purchase is a tax lien certificate, never the house itself. Until a circuit judge signs a foreclosure order, you can redeem. A sale also works, because the payoff on the lien is taken from the proceeds at settlement.

Selling checklist

A Howard sale has fewer layers than most, and this order keeps it moving.

  1. Look up your tax account and write down any unpaid balance and special rate.
  2. Get a payoff from Finance through the closing date if tax is overdue, since interest builds monthly.
  3. Agree in the contract on who pays the transfer and recordation taxes.
  4. Take the signed deed to the Division of Recordation Tax first, then to Land Records, or use e-recording.

What to bring to settlement

Have your photo ID, the latest tax bill, your lender's payoff letter if there is a mortgage, and any flood insurance records for a house near a stream. The county says consideration includes more than cash, so tell the title company about any credits or assumed debt so the taxes are figured on the right number. Because the recordation office closes at 4:30 p.m. and Land Records stops recording at 3:30 p.m., plan a same-day closing so the deed gets to both offices in time, or use e-recording to avoid the trip.

If the property needs repairs or has a tax lien, a cash sale as-is can close faster because the buyer is not waiting on a lender's appraisal. The title company still settles the county charges from your proceeds.

Frequently asked questions

When is Howard County property tax billed?

Real property tax is billed on July 1 each year. Many owners can choose two installments, and Finance can confirm the dates on your bill.

How much is the Howard County transfer tax?

Expect 1.25% of the price for the county, 0.5% more for the State, and recordation tax of $2.50 per $500.

Where do I record a deed in Howard County?

Start at the Division of Recordation Tax, 3430 Courthouse Drive, Ellicott City, to pay county taxes and have the deed stamped. Then record at Land Records, 9250 Judicial Way, Suite 1900, or through e-recording.

Do Howard County towns set their own property tax?

No. Howard has no incorporated municipalities, and SDAT lists a municipal rate of 0.0000. All real property tax comes through the county and the State.

What is the deadline to appeal in Howard County?

Forty-five days from the notice date. After the supervisor's hearing the appeals board gives you 30 days, and the Maryland Tax Court another 30 after its order.

Prince George's County at a glance

Prince George's County sits on the eastern side of Washington, D.C. The county seat is Upper Marlboro. The 2020 census counted 967,201 people, and the 2025 estimate is 970,374, which puts it second in Maryland by population.

Due dates and penalties

Each July the county sends bills, with full payment due September 30. Late payments add interest and a penalty, and not getting the bill is no defense. Tax years run from July 1 through June 30.

A house with open citations or unpermitted work can lose bids, so a seller who cannot fix them in time may prefer an as-is sale.

What a seller must disclose

Maryland Real Property Code section 10-702 requires the seller of a home with one to four units to hand the buyer either a disclosure or a disclaimer statement by the time the contract is signed. The disclaimer says the home is sold as-is, except for known latent defects.

Harford County for sellers

Harford County sits at the top of the Chesapeake Bay in northeastern Maryland. Bel Air is the county seat, and the Treasury and Revenue Collections offices are there. Aberdeen Proving Ground dwarfs every other employer at roughly 21,000 workers, which props up demand around Aberdeen and Edgewood.

Aberdeen, Bel Air and Havre de Grace run their own governments. Unincorporated communities such as Edgewood, Joppatowne, Fallston, Churchville and Belcamp cover much of the rest. Who bills the tax and what the rates are

Real estate tax is billed and collected by the county Treasury. The value comes from the State Department of Assessments and Taxation (SDAT). The Treasury is at 220 S. Main Street in Bel Air. Payment questions go to 410-638-3269 or treasury@harfordcountymd.gov.

Harford's rate has not moved from $0.9779 per $100 of assessed value across fiscal years 2023 to 2027. SDAT's 2026 to 2027 table adds the State rate of $0.1120 and shows a 5% homestead credit cap. Only the County Council can change the county's direct rates.

Those town numbers date from fiscal 2024. Phone the municipality for today's rate prior to telling a buyer.

How to appeal your assessment

The clock is 45 days from the date printed on your Notice of Assessment, which SDAT mails about every three years. Use the control number on the notice to file online, or send the paper form to the local assessment office.

  • Supervisor's level: a short informal hearing, typically 15 minutes, done on paper, by phone, on video or face to face.
  • Property Tax Assessment Appeals Board: 30 days after the final notice, free of charge.
  • Maryland Tax Court: 30 days after the board orders. You appear in person and the case is heard anew.
  • Petition for review: the route for the two years between reassessments, due the first working day after January 1.
  • Purchase appeal: a transfer after January 1 and before July 1 opens a 60 day window from the transfer date.

Tax owed at settlement is the billed amount, so an appeal in progress does not change the payoff figure.

The lien certificate and deed stamp

Before a transfer, Harford wants a Certificate of Tax Liens and Other Charges Due. It costs $50 (check payable to Harford County Government) and stays good for 90 days after issue. It covers real estate tax, water and sewer special assessments and other charges.

Title companies usually order it. An owner selling alone can mail the form to Bureau of Revenue Collections, P.O. Box 609, Bel Air, MD 21014. Ask Revenue Collections how long it will take, and apply well before your closing date.

Real Property Article 3-104 adds that taxes and assessments due have to be paid, and the collector's certificate endorsed on the deed, before the transfer is entered on the assessment books.

County staff also stamp every deed before it is recorded, whether or not tax is owed. Bring it to the Revenue Collections Office on weekdays between 8 a.m. and 5 p.m.; stamping usually takes 24 to 48 hours.

Transfer and recordation taxes

A Harford County deed carries a 1% county transfer tax, a 0.5% State transfer tax and a recordation tax of $6.60 per $1,000. County transfer tax proceeds are split evenly between farmland preservation and school costs. The Circuit Court collects the State transfer tax, and Revenue Collections collects the county pieces.

  • E-recording runs through Simplifile.
  • Claim an exemption by writing the full exemption code on the document; otherwise full tax applies.

Who pays each tax is set by the contract. Without an agreement, the law assumes the two sides split recordation and transfer taxes equally. A first-time Maryland buyer who will live in the house is the exception.

When property tax goes unpaid

Unpaid Harford County tax becomes eligible for the annual June tax sale about three months after it is overdue. In 2024 the county advertised 1,044 parcels owing about $2.33 million, and 282 parcels sold.

The county portion gains 1.5% a month and the State portion 1% a month, starting October 1 for a bill unpaid by September 30. Tax-sale preparation charges are added from May 1. A winning bidder gets a lien and not the house. You remain the owner and can redeem by paying off the lien, interest and fees.

Redemption is open until a circuit judge signs a foreclosure order. A purchaser in most counties cannot file to foreclose earlier than six months after the sale. Harford reported an installment plan under Tax-Property Article 10-209 and annual redemption interest of 12%.

Selling with tax owed

Selling ahead of the tax sale follows a short sequence.

  1. Order the lien certificate, or have your title company order it.
  2. Read the certificate for every charge, including water and sewer assessments.
  3. Pay the figure at closing from your proceeds, which clears the account.
  4. Have the deed stamped at Revenue Collections, then record it at Land Records.

A cash sale as-is can shorten this since no lender is waiting on repair items, and the payoff still comes out of the price. Keep the certificate's 90 day life in mind, and order a fresh one if your closing slips past it. Move before the annual sale if you want to avoid a lien auction.

What to have in hand: your latest tax bill, a copy of the deed, the contract of sale showing who pays transfer and recordation tax, and a check for the $50 certificate fee if you are applying yourself. If the house is inside Aberdeen, Bel Air or Havre de Grace, expect to visit the town office for its stamp before the county's. Planning for both stamps early keeps a closing date from slipping over a missing signature or stamp. If your buyer is financing, the lender and the title company will also want the certificate dated close to the closing, so do not order it too early.

Frequently asked questions

Who sends the Harford County property tax bill?

Treasury mails it, usually July 1. The state sets the assessed value, and the county applies its rate. Payment questions go to 410-638-3269.

Can I sell a Harford house with back taxes?

Yes. Settlement pays the balance, interest and any tax-sale charges out of the price, with the lien certificate stating the total. Closing ahead of the annual sale spares you a lien auction.

How long is the Harford County lien certificate good for?

Ninety days from issue. It costs $50 and is requested from the Bureau of Revenue Collections in Bel Air.

What is the Harford County transfer tax rate?

The county takes 1% of the price. State transfer tax adds 0.5%, or 0.25% when a first-time Maryland buyer will live there, and recordation runs $6.60 for every $1,000.

How do I contest my Harford County assessment?

Begin within 45 days of the notice date. If that fails, you can go to the Property Tax Assessment Appeals Board and then the Maryland Tax Court, neither of which charges to file.

Charles County at a glance

Charles County is in Southern Maryland. La Plata is the county seat, and Waldorf is the biggest community, with 81,410 residents in 2020. The county counted 166,617 people that year and an estimated 176,593 by 2025, a rise of 6.0 percent.

Waldorf works as a bedroom community for Washington, D.C., with MTA commuter bus routes 901, 903, 905 and 907 running between the two. The Indian Head naval installation on the Potomac is the largest single employer. Federal and base-related jobs can move a household on a fixed schedule, so some owners here want a closing date that will not slip.

Roughly 29 percent of the county's total area is water, so creeks, swamps and shoreline appear in many property descriptions.

Selling by area

Most Charles County sellers fall into one of four settings, and each has its own buyers and its own tax picture.

  • Waldorf: a large planned community on U.S. Route 301, where Maryland Route 5 begins.
  • La Plata: the county seat, a town with its own municipal rate.
  • Indian Head: a town tied to the naval base, also with its own municipal rate.
  • Rural Charles: Nanjemoy, Port Tobacco Village, Newburg, Bryantown and similar places, where lots are bigger, wells and septic systems are common, and water is never far off.

Towns charge a separate rate, so the same price can produce a very different bill depending on which side of a town line the house sits.

How property tax is billed

Real property tax here is billed and collected by the Treasurer. July is when full-year bills go out. Live in the house as your principal residence and you can pay in two parts: the first installment by September 30, and the second, plus a service charge, by December 31.

New construction and improvements generate supplemental bills, generally mailed in October (three-quarter year), January (half year) and April (quarter year). If your lender pays the tax from escrow, give it your bill and read the escrow analysis to confirm the payment was made.

  • Office: 200 Baltimore Street, La Plata, MD 20646. Mail goes to P.O. Box 2607.
  • Phone: 301-645-0685
  • Hours: weekdays from 8:00 a.m. to 4:30 p.m. The Waldorf payment center closes from 11:15 a.m. to 12:15 p.m. each day.
  • Assessment questions: SDAT sets values and answers at 301-932-2440.

Call the Treasurer for the current interest rate and service charge amount before you pay a late or split bill.

Tax rates by area

A house in unincorporated Charles County carried a combined real property rate of 1.2050 per $100 of value in the fiscal 2025 state figures, and towns stack their own rate over that.

The special rate of 0.0640 applies in the unincorporated area and in the towns listed. Port Tobacco totals 1.2450. You can test a bill with a calculator: take the taxable assessment, divide by 100, then multiply by the total rate.

Transfer and recordation tax

Maryland's local tax tables show Charles County with a 0.5 percent transfer tax and a recordation figure of $5.00 for fiscal 2025, rising to $7.00 for fiscal 2026. The final charges are printed on the settlement statement the title company prepares.

Credits and how to appeal

Charles County offers several credits, and SDAT reviews the applications. The list covers the Homestead Tax Credit, the Homeowners' Property Tax Credit (based on income), a senior tax credit and an exemption for 100 percent disabled former service members. Credits also exist for a perpetual conservation easement, for the surviving spouse of a fallen EMS officer and for volunteer emergency responders.

How to appeal your assessment

If the value looks too high, the state process applies here as it does everywhere in Maryland.

  1. First level: the Supervisor of Assessments, which must hear from you within 45 days of the date on the notice. The control number printed on the notice lets you file online, or you can mail a paper form.
  2. Second level: the Property Tax Assessment Appeals Board. You have 30 days from the Supervisor's final notice, and nothing is charged.
  3. Last level: the Maryland Tax Court, 30 days after the board rules. The hearing is held in person and the case is heard from scratch.

New owners get their own window. If the house changed hands from January 1 through June 30, the buyer has 60 days from the transfer date to appeal, provided the deed is recorded.

Flood zones and your sale

Charles County tries to keep its floodplain open so water can spread and drain downstream. A house inside a mapped Special Flood Hazard Area is treated differently from one outside it. Homeowners insurance does not cover flood damage, and owners can buy a National Flood Insurance Program policy through an insurance agent.

If your house sits near the Potomac, a creek or a swamp, expect the buyer's lender to ask about its flood zone. Look up your parcel on the FEMA map before listing, and keep any flood insurance paperwork where you can find it. A flood designation can pull offers down.

If the tax goes unpaid

When property tax is not paid, Maryland lets the county auction the debt as a lien. You still own the house, but whoever wins the auction can collect and, in time, ask a court to foreclose. Charles County holds its sale in May.

  • A notice goes out at least 30 days before the first advertisement, and the advertisement repeats weekly for four weeks.
  • Redemption stays open until a court ends it for good. Each month of delay adds cost.
  • A foreclosure filing can come six months after the sale, or nine for an owner-occupied home. If nothing is filed in two years, the certificate is void.

A house that sells before the auction usually has the tax paid by the title company from the proceeds. For help, the State Tax Sale Ombudsman answers at 410-767-4994, and its Homeowner Protection Program assists limited-income, elderly and disabled owners.

Clearing a tax balance at closing

A house with tax behind can still be sold. Get the Treasurer to quote what is owed through your planned closing date, give that quote to the title company, and the balance is deducted from what you receive. Aim to finish before the May sale if you can, because once a lien is auctioned the payoff grows with added costs.

Selling for cash avoids a buyer lender's appraisal and repair requests, which helps if the house needs work while interest piles up. Whichever route you take, bring the latest bill, any escrow statement from your lender and your photo ID to the first conversation with the title company.

Frequently asked questions

When is Charles County property tax due?

Full-year bills are mailed in July. Principal residence owners can pay in two parts, September 30 and December 31, with a service charge on the second. Call the Treasurer for the current interest rate.

Who do I call about a Charles County tax bill?

Dial 301-645-0685, or stop by 200 Baltimore Street in La Plata on a weekday. For the assessed value itself, call SDAT at 301-932-2440.

Why is La Plata taxed higher than the open county?

In the fiscal 2025 table, La Plata totals 1.4130 per $100 and the unincorporated area totals 1.2050. Indian Head totals 1.5060. The town adds its own rate, and figures reset yearly.

Can I sell with back tax owed?

Yes. Closing pays the tax from your proceeds, whether that happens before the auction or while the lien can still be redeemed. Get a payoff figure with a closing date attached, because interest and fees keep changing it.

How often is the tax sale?

Yes, in May. A property is sold only if the account is still unpaid when the sale comes around.

Westminster is the county seat and Eldersburg the largest community. The 2020 census counted 172,891 residents, with a 2025 estimate of 176,677. The terrain is rolling hills and forest, and the housing ranges from older downtown Westminster homes to newer subdivisions around Eldersburg. Due dates and discounts

A full-year payment and the first half of a split bill both come due July 1, and neither collects interest until after September 30. The second half is due December 1 and stays interest-free through December 31.

Paying the year in one check earns a discount of 1% by July 31 or 0.5% by August 31. Splitting the bill earns nothing, and the second half picks up a service charge unless both halves are paid by September 30.

  • The second installment becomes delinquent January 1.
  • The county will not waive interest or penalties for any reason or push back a due date.
  • A pending appeal or tax credit application does not change the due date.
  • A bill that never arrives does not excuse nonpayment, so request a duplicate.

Check your current bill for any changes to these dates.

The June tax sale

Each June the county auctions liens on unpaid real estate tax in an online sale through RealAuction, with proceedings starting around April 1.

Beginning May 1, overdue taxes can only be paid with cash, a certified check or a money order, and extra fees apply, so waiting until late April or May costs you the card and online options. Paying the current year does not shield you from legal action over unpaid prior years. The Collections Office links a Homeowner Protection Program page, so ask about eligibility if the sale is close.

Reading the town table before you list

Where the house sits decides the combined rate. Two houses with the same assessment can have very different bills if one is in Westminster at $1.6900 and the other in Mount Airy at $1.3262. A buyer's lender and agent will run the numbers by address, so know yours before you price the house. The homestead cap works the same way: it ranges from 3% in Mount Airy to 10% in Sykesville and Taneytown, and a cap only helps an owner who lives there and has applied for the credit.

If you rent the house out or it sits empty, the cap may not apply to you, and the buyer's bill could be higher or lower than yours depending on how they use it.

Planning a closing around the installments

Carroll's schedule gives sellers a few clear checkpoints. Before October 1 a full-year or first-installment bill is still interest-free. After that date it is delinquent, and a second installment turns delinquent January 1. Because the county does not waive interest or extend due dates, a closing that falls close to one of those dates should have the payment confirmed in writing by the Collections Office.

If you are selling before the year's taxes are fully paid, the title company will usually collect the unpaid portion from the proceeds. Tell your lender if taxes are escrowed, since the escrow account may already have paid part of the bill. Ask for a payoff that covers any lien and the days between your request and the closing date.

Credits and exemptions worth checking

A seller who has been in the house for years may already hold a credit that will not carry over to the buyer. The county's Senior Tax Credit serves homeowners 65 and older, and legally blind owners can claim a $15,000 assessment exemption, and a permanent 100% service-connected disability can qualify for a full exemption. The state credit and the Homeowner Protection Program add further options. Since each carries its own rules and paperwork, call the Collections Office at 410-386-2971 before you assume you still qualify, and mention the sale date when you do.

Weather and older houses

Westminster averages about 43 inches of precipitation and 20 inches of snow a year, so roofs, gutters and heating systems work hard. Buyers touring an older downtown house will check those first, so keep records of any recent roof or furnace work.

Selling with tax due

  2. Request a payoff from the Collections Office, along with the status of any lien.

  4. Give the title company a payoff request well before closing.

Is there a discount for paying Carroll County tax early?

Yes, for full-year payments only: 1% by July 31 and 0.5% by August 31. Semi-annual payments get no discount.

When is the Carroll County tax sale?

It is held online each June. From May 1, cash, certified check or money order is required.

Calvert County at a glance

Calvert County fills a peninsula in Southern Maryland between the Chesapeake Bay and the Patuxent River, with Prince Frederick as the county seat. Water covers roughly 38% of its 345 square miles, and the county includes five islands, Solomons Island and Broomes Island among them. Many residents commute toward Washington, and household incomes are high, which keeps demand for houses steady even when a property needs work.

A waterfront cottage in Chesapeake Beach and a ranch house on a wooded lot near Prince Frederick can have little in common when it comes to insurance, septic and upkeep, so describe yours in detail.

Tax rates by location

The county rate is $0.967 per $100 of assessed value and the state adds $0.112, for $1.079 per $100 in unincorporated areas. The fiscal 2027 county rate stays at 96.7 cents, the same as the year before. Because assessments rose, some bills still went up with the rate flat.

Billing, payment and the Treasurer's Office

The tax year runs July 1 through June 30, and owners of a principal residence can pay in two installments, September 30 and December 31. The second installment carries a service charge, so ask the Treasurer's Office for the amount. If no bill has reached you by August 31, request a duplicate. New construction is billed on a half-year basis from January 1 through June 30.

  • Online payments go through a vendor that charges 3.57% on cards, with a $5.18 minimum, or $2.59 for an e-check. The county does not keep the fee.
  • Partial payments are accepted only when the property is not in tax sale.
  • If a lender pays from escrow, forward the bill to the servicer and confirm payment on the annual escrow statement.
  • Address and residency changes go to the state assessment office, not the Treasurer.

The Treasurer's Office is at 150 Main Street, Prince Frederick, 410-535-1600. It handles tax liens and runs the annual tax sale.

Help for owners who are behind

The Homeowner Protection Program can pull a qualifying owner out of the tax sale process for three years. Requirements include a principal residence, an assessed value of $300,000 or less, household income of $60,000 or less, and non-dwelling assets of $200,000 or less.

The state Homeowners' Tax Credit is open to primary-residence owners with gross household income under $60,000, and applications go to the state. A Bay Restoration Fund hardship exemption lasts one year and must be renewed. These programs can lower what you owe before closing, and they can slow a tax sale long enough to list the house without a lien deadline hanging over you.

Building excise tax on new homes

Calvert charges a building excise tax on new residential construction, and it follows the property as a lien. A new single-family detached house totals $12,950, with $4,550 due at permit and $4,200 on each of the next two tax bills.

Other totals are $10,325 for a single-family attached unit, $9,050 for a manufactured home and $7,750 for an apartment. Later installments show up on the regular tax bill, so a buyer of a newly built home should ask whether any remain unpaid. The county enforces the tax like real property tax, with the same priority, interest and penalties for lien purposes. If you are selling a house built in the last two or three years, ask the Treasurer's Office what is left.

Roads, water and weather

Routes 4 and 2 meet at Sunderland and run together as Route 2-4, Solomons Island Road, through Prince Frederick, St. Leonard and Lusby. Route 260 runs southeast to Chesapeake Beach, and the Governor Thomas Johnson Bridge carries Route 4 into St. Mary's County. Summers are hot and humid and winters mild to chilly, so roofs and siding see the full range, and buyers of bay-side houses will look closely at both.

What to gather before you call the Treasurer

  • The tax ID number for your account, which the online portal uses to find your bills.
  • Your most recent bill, plus the one before it if a balance carries over.
  • Your mortgage servicer's name, if the lender pays from escrow.
  • For a newer house, the building permit date, so the office can tell you which excise installments are left.
  • Proof of income and assets if you want to ask about the Homeowner Protection Program or the state credit.

The office can tell you whether the account has been sent to tax sale. That single fact decides whether a partial payment is still possible, so ask it first.

Waterfront and older houses

Calvert's long shoreline means many sellers have docks, bulkheads, septic systems or houses close to the water. Buyers and their lenders ask about all of these, and a missing permit or an old system can slow a traditional sale. Collect whatever paperwork you have on repairs and upgrades. A cash offer is made on the house as it stands, so an aging septic tank or a tired deck is not something you have to resolve before closing, though the tax balance still gets paid from the proceeds.

Selling with tax due

  2. Ask the Treasurer's Office whether any amount has gone to tax sale, because partial payments stop once it has.
  3. Check your mortgage escrow so you do not pay twice.
  4. Ask the title company to order a payoff through your closing date.

If the house also needs repairs you cannot afford, selling as is lets unpaid tax come out of the proceeds at settlement instead of sitting on the account. Call or text us with the address and we will tell you what we can offer.

What is the Calvert County real estate tax rate?

The county rate is $0.967 per $100 of assessed value, unchanged for fiscal 2027. With the state's $0.112, unincorporated areas pay $1.079 per $100.

When are Calvert County property taxes due?

Owners of a principal residence may pay in two installments due September 30 and December 31. The second carries a service charge.

What is the homestead cap in Calvert County?

Taxable increases on an owner-occupied home are capped at 10% a year effective July 1, 2026, if you have applied for the credit.

Can I get out of a Calvert County tax sale?

The Homeowner Protection Program can remove a qualifying owner from the tax sale process for three years. The county sets income, asset and assessed value limits.

Does a new Calvert County house carry an extra tax?

Yes. The county building excise tax on a new single-family detached house totals $12,950, paid in three installments, and it is a lien until paid.

Worcester County at a glance

Worcester is the only Maryland county with an Atlantic coastline. It fills the state's far southeast corner, shares borders with both Delaware and Virginia, and has Snow Hill as its county seat. The land is flat and low, with barrier islands offshore and the Pocomoke River swamp to the south.

When are Worcester County property taxes due?

The yearly bill is issued in July. Anything unpaid on October 1 is delinquent and picks up interest at 1 percent a month. Paper copies go out in the mail early in July, and the online version is posted from July 1.

A July payment of the whole County tax earns a 0.5 percent discount. Owners of a principal residence, along with businesses whose tax is $100,000 or less, may split the bill. Half is delinquent after October 1, the rest is due December 1, and late interest on that half starts January 1. Newly built homes receive a six-month bill every January.

Mind the mail. The Treasurer must have your money in hand by month end, and a postmark counts for nothing, so a check sent close to a deadline can land late and still be charged.

  • October 1: a full-year bill or first half left unpaid becomes delinquent.
  • October 1: last day to apply for the Homeowner's Tax Credit.

Assessments, appeals and credits

Valuation is a state job. Each owner gets a notice with the previous and updated value on a three-year schedule. In the most recent round, Worcester residential values moved by 10.5 percent, and any increase is stretched across three years.

Someone buying between January 1 and July 1 gets 60 days counted from the transfer, once the deed is recorded. Forms are on the SDAT appeal page.

Two credits are worth asking about. The Homeowner's Tax Credit is income-based and has to be claimed again each year before October 1. The county Homestead Tax Credit needs no application: it kicks in on its own when an owner-occupied assessment jumps beyond the set percentage.

Unpaid taxes and the annual tax sale

Delinquent accounts end up at a lien sale that Worcester holds every late spring. A bill that never reached you is no defense. By state law, real property tax is a lien on the house from the day it is due.

Calling the Treasurer early matters, since the 1 percent monthly interest keeps adding up.

Selling a house that owes tax takes three moves. Request a payoff through the day you plan to close. Pass it to the title company. At settlement the tax is deducted from what you receive, and the buyer gets a clean title.

Transfer and recordation costs when selling

Three charges attach to a Worcester deed. Recordation is 0.66 percent, the county transfer tax is 0.5 percent, and the state transfer tax is 0.5 percent, so deeds bear 1.66 percent in all. When the buyer will occupy the home at least 7 months a year, the opening $50,000 is excused from the county transfer tax.

Recordation tax goes to the Treasurer for any document submitted after December 31, 2024, and checks are made out to Worcester County. Call 410-632-0686 and pick option 3 with questions. Percentages shift over time, so let the title company verify them before you agree to a price.

Selling a Worcester County house fast

Putting a house on the market reaches the most buyers, yet an inherited beach unit can sit while heirs untangle paperwork and payoffs. Selling for cash as-is removes the appraisal and any buyer loan, so you choose the closing day.

  • Print the latest bill from Taxes Online.
  • Get a payoff from the Treasurer and see whether a credit or the July discount changes the balance.
  • Look for your town in the rate table to learn if a second bill exists.
  • Locate the deed and a mortgage statement.

Our offers cover Worcester County homes in any shape. Set one next to a listing's likely net after repairs, commission and holding costs. Saying no costs you nothing.

Closing day is when the pieces meet. The title company collects the payoff from your proceeds, the transfer and recordation charges are paid, and the deed is recorded. A seller who has already asked the Treasurer for a payoff, checked the town rate and confirmed any credit will see no surprises on the settlement sheet.

Bills are issued in July. A balance still open on October 1 is delinquent and draws 1 percent interest monthly. Two-payment owners owe the second half December 1.

Is there a discount for paying Worcester County taxes early?

Yes. Pay the whole County tax in July and take 0.5 percent off the County portion.

Where is the Worcester County Treasurer's Office?

Snow Hill, in Room 1105 at 1 West Market Street, with a branch counter at the Isle of Wight Center in Bishopville. Doors open weekdays from 8:00 a.m. until 4:30 p.m.

Does the county collect Ocean City property tax?

Yes, it bills and collects for the town, at $0.4326 per $100 of assessed value.

Can I sell a Worcester County house with unpaid property tax?

You can. The lien is paid off from your proceeds at closing, so request a fresh payoff from the Treasurer before choosing a date.

The elderly and disabled deferral is the one that changes a closing. It postpones only the year-over-year increase in county tax. What was postponed gets recorded as a lien, and it comes due when you sell or move.

Online, every June. The 2025 sale opened for bids May 31 and wrapped up in early June.

Yes. A deferred amount is recorded as a lien and has to be repaid when the owner sells or moves out.

Water makes up 53% of the county's area, and the shoreline runs more than 500 miles. That matters when you sell, because coastal bluffs protect many areas from storm surge while low-lying land and tidal marshes are more exposed.

The State Department of Assessments and Taxation values the property. The St. Mary's County Treasurer sends and collects the bill at 23150 Leonard Hall Drive, Leonardtown, phone 301-475-4200, extension 3300.

Maryland Route 235 and Route 5 are the main state highways, with Routes 4, 6, 234 and 245 also serving the county. What does not go away is the paperwork: well testing under Section 10-713 unless the buyer waives it in writing, any septic inspection the county requires, and payoff of every tax and utility lien.

If you inherited the house, confirm who has authority to sign before you talk to buyers. Several heirs can slow a closing more than price does. Line up every signature early, and keep the estate paperwork with your closing documents.

The county holds its annual tax sale on the first Friday of March for the prior tax year.

File within 45 days of the notice date with the local assessment office. Later levels are the Property Tax Assessment Appeals Board and the Maryland Tax Court, each with a 30 day window.

Talbot County at a glance

Talbot County sits on Maryland's Eastern Shore, with the Chesapeake Bay along its western side and Easton as the county seat. Roughly 44 percent of its 477 square miles is water, and the Choptank, Miles, Wye and Tred Avon rivers cut deep into the land. That is why so many Talbot properties sit on a creek, a cove or river frontage, and why lenders sometimes ask about the shoreline, the road access and the survey.

Town lines drive the bill. A house inside Easton, Oxford, St. Michaels, Trappe or Queen Anne carries a municipal levy in addition to county and state charges, while an unincorporated address owes just the county and state portions.

Who handles property tax

Your value comes from one place and your bill from another. The state assessments department (SDAT) decides what the house is worth for tax purposes and takes first-round appeals. The county Finance Office mails the bill, takes payment and conducts the yearly lien sale.

Walk in at the Talbot County Courthouse, 11 North Washington Street, Suite 9, Easton, or call 410-770-8020. Online, the self-service portal linked from the county tax information page shows a bill and accepts payment.

Due dates and penalties

Bills open on July 1, and you can pay with no interest until September 30. From October 1, the county adds interest and penalties of one percent for each month or partial month that the balance stays open.

A house you live in qualifies for a split: half by September 30 and half by December 31. The second half comes with a service charge, which a single full payment by September 30 avoids. That charge tops out at 1.279 percent of what remains unpaid in December.

Selling in the fall? Ask the Finance Office whether the first half is in and whether a service charge is on the account. Your closing agent will need the exact balance.

How are assessments set, and how do you appeal?

Every property is revalued once in three years, and SDAT mails a Notice of Assessment with the old and new market value. In the 2026 round, Talbot County residential values changed by 18.2 percent. What happens if taxes go unpaid?

Taxes you do not pay attach to the house as a lien. Tax-Property Article section 14-804 makes state, county and town real property tax a lien from the due date until it is paid, and Talbot sells those liens each late spring at its tax sale.

Owners keep the right to redeem after a lien sale by paying the back taxes and fees. Treat the sale as a warning and not as the end. The debt keeps growing, though, and a title company will insist it be cleared before closing.

Owners with low income can apply to the Homeowner Protection Program. It can hold a home out of tax sale for three years or longer and help with the balance. Reach the State Tax Sale Ombudsman at 410-767-4994 or sdat.taxsale@maryland.gov.

A Talbot deed carries three charges: county transfer tax, state transfer tax and recordation tax. County code puts the first at 1 percent of the price, with the opening $50,000 exempt. The Clerk of the Circuit Court takes payment before recording the deed.

Recordation runs 1.2 percent here and the state transfer tax 0.5 percent, which together with the county's 1 percent makes 2.7 percent on a deed. First-time Maryland buyers of a principal residence get a lower state rate of 0.25 percent, and the seller pays that. Your contract decides who covers the rest.

Rates move, so get the exact numbers from the title company on your settlement sheet. Any back tax comes out of your proceeds at the table, which lowers what you walk away with.

Selling with taxes owed, or an inherited house

An inherited Talbot house can arrive with a tax bill, a lien and nobody living in it. A sale can still happen. The order of steps helps:

  1. Request a payoff from the Finance Office, service charge included, valid through your intended closing day.
  2. Look up the SDAT record for the assessed value and any appeal still open.
  3. Find out whether a town bills the address as well.

Frequently asked questions

When are property taxes due in Talbot County, Maryland?

Bills open July 1 and are interest-free through September 30. Penalties begin October 1. A home you live in may be paid half by September 30 and half by December 31.

Where do I pay Talbot County property tax?

Pay at the Finance Office inside the courthouse at 11 North Washington Street, Suite 9, Easton, or use the county's online portal. Call 410-770-8020 with questions.

How long do I have to appeal a Talbot County assessment?

The deadline is 45 days after the date printed on the Notice of Assessment. Buyers who take title between January 1 and July 1 get 60 days after the transfer, once the deed is recorded.

Does Talbot County have a transfer tax?

Yes, at 1 percent of the price with the first $50,000 exempt, collected by the Clerk of the Circuit Court. A state transfer tax and a recordation tax come on top.

Can I sell a Talbot County house that is behind on taxes?

Yes. The lien is settled out of your proceeds at closing. Get a payoff figure from the Finance Office before picking a closing date.

Dorchester County in brief

Dorchester sits on the Mid-Eastern Shore of Maryland. Cambridge is its seat and biggest city. The 2020 census counted 32,531 people, and the 2025 estimate is 33,628. Cambridge had 13,096 residents, and 13.9 percent of its 6,464 housing units were empty.

With about 33,600 residents countywide, buyers come from a small local pool, and many properties are rural parcels, waterfront lots or older town houses. Water covers 442 of the county's 983 square miles, which shapes both pricing and insurance.

Flood zones and your sale

About 55 percent of the land in Dorchester County sits in the 1 percent annual chance floodplain, and nearly 75 percent is below 20 feet in elevation. Those figures come from the county's 2022 Flood Mitigation Plan update.

  • A 1% flood would affect 2,440 buildings countywide, with about $37.1 million in estimated losses.
  • In the City of Cambridge, 126 buildings would be affected, about $2.65 million in losses.
  • The county has 54 repetitive loss properties in the unincorporated areas and Cambridge, plus 3 severe repetitive loss properties.
  • Hurricane Isabel in 2003 pushed storm surge over 8 feet in some areas, and Tropical Storm Isaias in 2020 brought a federal major disaster declaration.

Church Creek, Eldorado and Galestown lie fully within storm surge zones. If your house is near the water, buyers will ask about elevation, flood insurance and past claims. Gather elevation certificates, insurance declarations and any claim history before listing so the buyer's lender has less to stall on.

How property tax is billed

July is when bills are mailed. A full annual bill, or the first half of a split one, is due September 30, and the second half is due December 31. One county office collects real property tax for every municipality inside the county.

Payment options are the online Tax and Utility Bill portal, the mail, or the County Office Building at 501 Court Lane in Cambridge. The county main number is 410-228-1700, and the Department of Finance answers at 410-228-4343. The office closes for Thanksgiving, Christmas, New Year's Day and Martin Luther King Jr. Day.

After the due dates, unpaid accounts gain interest and a penalty, and the lien can move toward the county's tax sale. Interest runs monthly, so ask Finance for a payoff figure on the exact day you plan to close.

Tax rates in Dorchester County and Cambridge

A Cambridge house carries a far higher combined rate than a similar one in the open county. If you own both a town house and a rural parcel, compare the two bills before deciding which to list first.

Transfer and recordation tax

State tables list a county transfer tax of 0.75 percent and a recordation tax figure of $5.00. The title company works out the real charge from the deed and the price, and prints it on the settlement statement.

The Dorchester County tax sale

The county runs its tax sale online. In 2025 bidding opened at noon on June 16 and closed at noon on June 17, so expect a mid-June window and confirm the date with the finance office each year.

  • The 2025 sale covered unpaid taxes and fees for tax years 2023 to 2024 and 2024 to 2025.
  • Bidders registered online for a $50 fee.
  • Paying in full by 4:00 p.m. on June 12, 2025 pulled a property out of the sale.
  • Owners also owe a $50 advertising fee per property, plus interest as the law provides.

State rules let you redeem until a court forecloses. Foreclosure can be requested six months after the sale, nine for an owner-occupied home, and a certificate with no case filed in two years becomes void.

Appeals and claims

An owner in Dorchester climbs the same three-rung appeal ladder as everyone else in Maryland, and the first rung closes 45 days after the notice date. SDAT revalues property roughly every third year and mails each owner a Notice of Assessment.

  1. Start with the Supervisor of Assessments and file within 45 days of the notice date.
  2. Next comes the Property Tax Assessment Appeals Board, which needs your request within 30 days.
  3. Last is the Maryland Tax Court, 30 days after the board issues its order.

Between reassessments, you can file a petition for review no later than the first working day after January 1. Someone who buys after January 1 and before July 1 gets 60 days from the transfer date, once the deed is on record. If you are selling in that window, tell your buyer the option exists. It costs nothing to raise and can lower their bill later.

Selling with taxes owed

An unpaid tax bill does not block a sale. Settle the balance ahead of the cutoff and the house drops off the list. Miss it, and the lien can still be paid out of your proceeds at closing, only with extra fees and interest in the total.

  1. Call the finance office and ask for the total through your closing date.
  2. Ask whether the town also bills separately, which matters in Cambridge and Hurlock.
  3. Hand the payoff to the title company so it lands on the settlement statement.
  4. Keep the paid receipt in case the buyer's lender asks.

Timing around the sale list

The tax sale covers accounts that are still unpaid in the spring and early summer, so the best time to clear a balance is before then, when only interest is running. After advertising begins, the $50 advertising fee per property is added. Waiting until the last day leaves no room for a bank wire to clear or a check to be posted, so give yourself a few days of cushion before the cutoff. If a buyer is financing, the lender will want proof that the tax is current before it funds, and an unpaid balance will delay that approval.

Cash buyers tend to close sooner than financed ones, useful when a sale date looms. A flood-prone or older house also tends to run into lender appraisal issues that a cash purchase avoids.

Frequently asked questions

When are Dorchester County property taxes due?

The annual bill and first installment are due September 30, and the second installment is due December 31. Interest and a penalty start once those dates pass.

How much of Dorchester County is in a floodplain?

About 55 percent of the county's land lies in the 1 percent annual chance floodplain, and nearly 75 percent is under 20 feet in elevation.

What is the property tax rate in Cambridge?

The fiscal 2025 total is 1.7363 per $100, made of a 0.9267 county rate and a 0.8096 town rate. Unincorporated Dorchester County totals 1.0000, so check the current year before you rely on these numbers.

Can I sell a Dorchester County house before the tax sale?

Yes. Pay the tax and fees before the cutoff and the house leaves the sale list, or let closing pay the balance from proceeds. In 2025 the payment deadline was June 12 at 4:00 p.m., so ask the finance office for the current date.

What is the Dorchester County transfer tax?

State tables show 0.75 percent for fiscal 2025 and 2026. Who pays, and any exemptions, depend on the contract and the deed, so confirm with the title company.
